report.headline: NBA->EuroLeague move projects a modest usage bump to 25.9%, but the shooting-efficiency projection is not trustworthy

projection.text: Usage rate is projected to rise to 25.9% in the EuroLeague (80% interval 21.2%–30.6%), up from 20.9% in the NBA and above the receiving league's 20.2% average; the parallel true-shooting projection of 53.6% should not be read as informative because the model underperforms a simple league-average baseline on that metric.

risks.text: The true-shooting projection of 53.6% cannot be trusted: the model's error (4.5%) is larger than the trivial league-mean baseline's error (4.3%) on this metric.
Source-season true shooting was 49.0%, which stood at -1.46 sd relative to the NBA that year — a substantial efficiency deficit heading into the move.

Players who historically made this NBA->EL transition sat -0.31 sd below their own league's average, unlike the more typical pattern of movers being above average, which raises questions about how representative the 115-transition estimate is for this player.
The 95% prediction interval for usage rate runs from 18.7% to 33.0%, a span of more than three EuroLeague standard deviations (4.7%), reflecting substantial individual-level unpredictability.

strengths.text: Usage rate is projected to climb from 20.9% in the NBA (+0.15 sd) to 25.9% in the EuroLeague, above the league's 20.2% average, suggesting a larger role after the move.
On usage rate specifically, the model beats the best trivial baseline (3.2% mean absolute error vs 4.2%), so this projection carries genuine signal.
The fitted carryover slope for usage rate is 0.977, meaning a player's standing above their league's average usage tends to transfer almost fully across this transition type.
In the source season the player produced 15.311 points, 1.807 assists, and 4.352 rebounds per 75 possessions on a 20.9% usage rate, indicating an established offensive role in the NBA.

uncertainty.text: The 80% prediction interval for usage rate spans 21.2%–30.6%, a range of roughly two EuroLeague standard deviations (4.7%), so the model can rank this player against peers but cannot pin down a precise figure, and the 95% interval widens further to 18.7%–33.0%; the true-shooting projection carries even less weight, since the model's held-out error (4.5%) is worse than the trivial league-mean baseline (4.3%) on that metric.
